problem: v3.15 uses exactly 100 yen per ticket for all JRA main race purchase commands; 100 yen is the minimum JRA unit, not generally the optimal capital allocation.
scope: STEP2 variable-stake research after the existing v3.15 frozen purchase set; no STEP1/marks, actual quotes, selection or operation-count changes.
objective: Maximize modeled CENTRAL expected net profit among bounded JRA purchase-command-level 100-yen stake grids, subject to low-scenario profit and modeled net-loss-probability gates. No claim of globally optimal ticket selection or model calibration.

models: v3.13 SHA-pinned prereace joint finish outcome distributions
v3.15 published purchase commands and quotes
safeguards.proof_chain: v3.13 prediction SHA256+Git proof must match sealed v3.15 source SHA256+proof; recompute exact v3.15 published baseline portfolio statistics
safeguards.purchased_ticket_identity: no deletion, substitution or new tickets; duplicate-free verified official odds only
safeguards.purchase_command_limit: same maximum 3 regular and optional one medium + one large
safeguards.stake_size: 100-yen increments per entire purchase command, uniform across expanded combination tickets
safeguards.side_ticket_handling: both speculative 中穴 and 大穴 remain 100 yen, no staking up
safeguards.baseline_low_net_loss_probability: may increase by at most 0.5 percentage points
safeguards.unspent_money: left unspent when no candidate passes safety gates
safeguards.deployment: none: no change to canonical races.json or formal request, prediction, HTML, PDF, Git proof or public site

future_milestones: Run synthetic invariant and proof-chain tests and three frozen prestart replay comparisons, logging stake, central/low EV, central/low loss probability, hit probability and exact JRA purchase command unit prices.
Independently validate replays on multiple previous JRA weeks; evaluate calibration error and how results change with lower/upper outcome-scenario probabilities.
Assess out-of-sample realized performance only after races finish, without using results to rewrite prestart predictions or shadow stakes.
Propose formal promotion only after safety and regression gates pass, with user approval for affected purchase-policy changes. Retain historical versions unchanged.
benchmark.formal_promotion_requires: explicit follow-up approval and new versioned implementation after multi-week study; do not silently activate the candidate
benchmark.insufficient_evidence: one day / three races are a smoke test, not evidence that the staking policy consistently performs better
